title: Realtime quota watermarking and idempotent billing sink
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a real-time quota reconciliation and billing sink that uses event watermarks and idempotent writes to ensure tenant token accounting is correct in the presence of out-of-order and late-arriving usage events. Goal: eliminate transient double-charges and reduce reconciliation lag from minutes to seconds for hosted API and Dedicated routes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline handles late-arriving events up to 10 minutes with deterministic ordering via watermarks
Billing sink writes are idempotent and tolerant to at-least-once delivery from the stream consumer
Unit/per-tenant deviation from canonical ledger < 0.1% after 1 minute of event arrival in synthetic tests
Canary run for 5% of production traffic with automatic rollback on imbalance > 1%
Comprehensive dashboards: per-route error-rate, watermark lag, idempotency conflicts resolved
technical_notes: Architecture: event stream -> watermark assignment -> per-tenant aggregation window -> dedupe + idempotent sink -> canonical ledger store
Watermark strategy: hybrid event-time with periodic punctuations from ingestion layer; advance watermark only when healthy at shard level
Idempotency keys: use (tenant_id, route_id, request_id, ingestion_shard, sequence) hashed into stable 128-bit key to avoid collisions
Sink semantics: upsert-style writes to ledger with compare-and-swap on last_sequence_applied; fallback to tombstone+reapply for cross-shard races
Backpressure: use adaptive batching with size/time thresholds tuned per-shard; prefer smaller batches for high-latency tenants
Observability: emit watermark_lag_ms, late_event_rate, idempotency_hits, write_conflicts per tenant and globally
Failure mode: if watermark stalls for >30s mark shard degraded and route to best-effort path; operations runbook created
Compatibility: must interoperate with existing cost allocation fanout and chargeback jobs without schema change
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Verified watermarking approach in local Flink prototype; handled 6% late events in synthetic replay without misordering.
2025-02-18: Design review with PM and Storage. Decided to implement idempotent sink using a CAS column in tenant_ledger table rather than external redis lease to minimize operational surface.
2025-02-24: Prototype PR opened for per-tenant windowing and watermark punctuations (github.com/redwood-inference/inc/PR-4201). Initial benchmarks show 25k writes/s per partition.
2025-03-01: Integration test failures observed for cross-shard retries; added a tombstone-and-reapply flow in prototype to resolve sequence gaps. New integration tests added.

2025-03-03: Load test on staging with 10% production traffic. Watermark lag median 400ms, p95 1.8s. Still seeing idempotency conflicts at 0.02% for high-concurrency tenants; investigating metric tagging improvements.
comments: PM review (Ravi Sharma, 2025-02-13): Love the CAS-based sink idea. Please add a canary gating plan and explicit impact on billing pipeline latency.
Design feedback (Nina Gordon, 2025-02-19): Concern about tombstone growth in ledger table. Recommend TTL compaction job and archived sequence checkpoints.
Storage lead (Ola Johansson, 2025-02-25): CAS column approach OK, but ensure schema migration is zero-downtime and limit VACUUM churn. We'll schedule a migration window.
SRE note (Keisha Brown, 2025-03-02): Add alert for watermark_retention_exceeded and create an automated rollback playbook to flip traffic to best-effort aggregator.
Engineering comment (Miguel Alvarez, 2025-03-03): Experimenting with batch size tuning to reduce idempotency conflict rate; next step is adjusting punctuations frequency from ingestion layer.
